draft.title: Comparing scores with z-scores
card: Raw scores from different tests cannot be compared directly, because each test has its own mean and spread. A mark of 70 can be good on one test and weak on another.
A z-score fixes this. z = (score − mean) ÷ standard deviation. It shows how many standard deviations a score is above or below its own group's mean.
Work out the z-score for each test. The higher z-score is the better performance relative to the group. A negative z-score means below the mean.
Example: Maths 72 (mean 60, SD 8) gives z = 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5. Science 68 (mean 50, SD 12) gives z = 18 ÷ 12 = 1.5. The two performances are equal relative to their groups.
draft.remember: Convert each score to a z-score. The higher z-score is the better result for its group.

a.q: Ravi scores 64 in English (mean 55, SD 6) and 58 in History (mean 50, SD 4). In which subject did he do better relative to the group?
opts: History, because its z-score is 2 and English is 1.5
English, because its z-score is 1.5 and History is 2
English, because 64 is higher than 58
History, because its mean is lower than English
a.why: English z = 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5. History z = 8 ÷ 4 = 2. The higher z-score means a better result for the group. Comparing raw marks is tempting, but each test has its own mean and spread.
a.clue: Find a z-score for each subject, then compare them.

b.q: Priya scores 45 on a music test (mean 38, SD 5) and 81 on a drama test (mean 70, SD 10). Which statement is correct?
opts: Music was better: z = 1.4 compared with z = 1.1
Drama was better: z = 1.1 compared with z = 1.4
Drama was better, as she was 11 marks above the mean
The two were equal, because both are above the mean
b.why: Music z = 7 ÷ 5 = 1.4. Drama z = 11 ÷ 10 = 1.1. Drama has the bigger gap from the mean in marks, but the spread is wider, so that gap is fewer standard deviations. Music is the better result for its group.
b.clue: Divide each gap from the mean by that test's standard deviation.

a.best: History, because its z-score is 2 and English is 1.5

b.best: Music was better: z = 1.4 compared with z = 1.1

proposal.title: Comparing scores with z-scores
card: Raw scores from different tests cannot be compared directly, because each test has its own mean and spread. A mark of 70 can be strong on one test and weak on another.
To compare, convert each score to a z-score using its own test's mean and standard deviation (SD). This puts both scores on the same scale.
The higher z-score is the better performance relative to its group. A bigger gap in marks does not always give a higher z-score, because a wider spread makes it smaller.
Example: Maths 72 (mean 60, SD 8) gives z = (72 − 60) ÷ 8 = 1.5. Science 68 (mean 50, SD 12) gives z = (68 − 50) ÷ 12 = 1.5. The two results are equal relative to their groups.
proposal.remember: Compare z-scores, not raw marks. The higher z-score is the better result for its group.
